findings.title: OpenCode upper bound keyed by directory only
findings.problem: sameTranscriptKeys matches opencode and codemie-code records on working directory alone, so two concurrent records in one directory count as covering the same transcript even when their native sessions differ. Outside a hook process that bound now reaches MetricsWriter.appendDeltas.
findings.impact: After a second record starts, the earlier record's own deltas can be dropped as after_end, and the drop is permanent because the bound stays. Reachability was unconfirmed: the OpenCode adapter's use of the native id was not read within the budget.
findings.recommendation: Key opencode and codemie-code records by their native session id when the record has one, falling back to the directory only when it does not, so a concurrent record over another native session bounds nothing. Add a test with two records in one directory.

findings.title: Kimi records get no upper bound
findings.problem: kimi and kimi-acp reach the default branch of sameTranscriptKeys, which returns no keys, so nextRecordStart gives Kimi no later-record bound. The docs promise this bound through the shared writer.
findings.impact: When a Kimi record resumes a wire transcript another record covers, a late non-hook pass of the earlier record can claim the later record's deltas. Reachability was unconfirmed: whether a Kimi record's correlation names its file was not read.
findings.recommendation: Add kimi and kimi-acp cases keyed by correlation.agentSessionFile, and cover the later-record bound in the Kimi window test.

findings.title: Core and plugins import SSO lock module
findings.problem: architecture.md:152-155 lists Core depending on Plugins and direct Plugin-to-Plugin calls as anti-patterns. run-window.ts and session-generation.ts now import lock code and types from src/providers/plugins/sso, and six agent plugins import appendSessionFile from there. Similar imports exist at base, so this extends a pattern.
findings.impact: The new shared locking contract makes agent core and six agent plugins depend on one provider plugin, against the architecture check in the git-workflow.md review checklist.
findings.recommendation: Move locked-jsonl.ts and the RunWindow and LockBounds types, with the JSONL helpers they need, to a lower layer such as src/agents/core/session or src/utils, and have the callers import them from there.

findings.title: Metrics processors ignore AppendResult
findings.problem: appendDeltas can write fewer deltas than it is given, and when the file is gone it returns written:0 with no flag to separate that from nothing new. Claude, Kimi, Codex, OpenCode and Copilot call sites confirmed here still report deltas.length (or their own batch) as written. Conversation processors got a dropped-write branch; metrics processors did not.
findings.impact: Logs and metadata claim deltas that never reached disk. sync-state-utils.ts:44 accumulates totalDeltas from those counts and persists processed ids, so sync state overstates what was written and drops are hidden.
findings.recommendation: Use AppendResult.written for logs, deltasWritten, recordsProcessed and totalDeltas in every metrics processor, expose the dropped-because-gone case in AppendResult, and add a processor-level test that those fields match the writer after a drop.

findings.title: Kimi resolves window for an empty batch
findings.problem: Kimi calls resolveRunWindow and appendDeltas even when newDeltas is empty, unlike Codex and Copilot, which guard on deltas.length, and Claude, which returns early. That adds a record lookup, a later-record scan and a lock acquisition to a pass with nothing to write.
findings.impact: A missing record or a lock timeout fails a pass that has nothing to do, returning success:false where it previously succeeded. Gemini and Pi call sites have the same shape as far as read; their earlier returns were not checked.
findings.recommendation: Guard the call with newDeltas.length > 0 as Codex and Copilot do, and confirm the same guard exists on the Gemini and Pi paths.

findings.title: Lower bound can drop a record's own deltas
findings.problem: A delta whose time precedes record.startTime is dropped at debug level only. This assumes a record never starts after its own lines, which is checked nowhere: several fixtures moved startTime back to keep passing. parseDeltaTime also assumes numeric times are epoch milliseconds, and Kimi passes event.time through unconverted.
findings.impact: A record created after its first transcript line, such as a discovered session, or a time in seconds, would lose those deltas with no warning. Reachability was unconfirmed: the review budget ended before Desktop record creation and Kimi's time unit were read.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that every record's startTime precedes its own transcript lines, including discovered Claude Desktop records, and that every numeric delta time is epoch milliseconds (Kimi's event.time passes through unconverted). Log before_start drops at warn level, and normalise or exempt whatever fails either check.

findings.title: Synthesized delta time hits the upper bound
findings.problem: Processors fall back to Date.now() when a line has no time (copilot-cli.metrics-processor.ts:85 and :92, kimi.metrics-processor.ts:216, opencode.metrics-processor.ts:394). The writer judges that synthesized time as real, so reprocessing an earlier record after a later one started puts it past upperBound.
findings.impact: A delta in the record's own window is dropped as after_end, against the writer's rule that a delta with no usable time is kept. Reachability was unconfirmed: how often these lines lack a time was not established.
findings.recommendation: Do not judge a synthesized time: leave the time unusable or mark the delta at the fallback sites, so appendDeltas skips the window check for it, matching the writer's rule that a delta with no usable time is kept.

findings.title: 20 000-line append test misses stated bound
findings.problem: The PR lists a test for one delta at 20 000 lines under 100 ms. Per the acceptance lens the test asserts toBeLessThan(1000), ten times that bound. Not re-verified: the review budget ended first.
findings.impact: The read-per-append cost the bound exists to limit can grow tenfold with the test still green, and the description overstates what is guarded.
findings.recommendation: Align the test and the PR description: assert the stated 100 ms if it is reliable on CI, otherwise correct the description to the bound the test enforces.

findings.title: Lock timeout after upload invites a resend
findings.problem: The final rewrite runs after the server has accepted the batch and has no local catch, and it gains a new failure mode: SessionFileLockTimeoutError after the 10 s budget. Outcomes are held only in memory, so a timeout loses them. When the file is gone, the sync warns and still reports success.
findings.impact: Accepted deltas stay pending on disk and a later pass can send them again, double-counting analytics. It needs the lock held past 10 s, which is uncommon but live; a dead holder with a reused pid in a hook process is one route. Whether the server dedupes resends was not checked.
findings.recommendation: Catch SessionFileLockTimeoutError around the final rewrite and keep the outcome so it is applied on a retry or the next pass, so sent deltas are not sent again. Report the outcome as not persisted rather than as a failed sync.
